s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and discharge of the right upper eyelid with underlying sinus involvement
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Discharge of pus for the previous 10 months
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Opacification and expansion of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Discharge of pus for the previous 10 months
No trauma to the head
No symptoms such as fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node, 11 × 7 mm, on the right upper eyelid
High signal on T2-weighted MRI and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
Opacification and expansion of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, and few eosinophils on histopathology
No sign of malignancy on histopathology

shortlist.label: Chronic frontal sinusitis with cutaneous fistula
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of chronic swelling and discharge of the right upper eyelid with underlying sinus involvement

shortlist.label: Pott's puffy tumor with sinocutaneous fistula
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses

shortlist.label: Chronic sinusitis with mucocele and cutaneous fistula
shortlist.why_kept: Explains the presence of a scarlike node on the right upper eyelid discharging pus

shortlist.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Supported by the MRI findings of high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus

shortlist.label: Sinusitis-induced orbital abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the proximity of the sinuses to the orbit and the potential for infection spread

s4.champion: Chronic frontal sinusitis with cutaneous fistula

raw.champion: Chronic frontal sinusitis with cutaneous fistula
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid with discharge of pus, combined with imaging findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus and histopathology showing mild inflammatory infiltrate without malignancy, best supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pott's puffy tumor with sinocutaneous fistula
rejected.why: Typically presents with more severe symptoms such as fever and headache, which are absent in this case

rejected.label: Chronic sinusitis with mucocele and cutaneous fistula
rejected.why: Mucocele is not explicitly indicated by the imaging or histopathology findings

rejected.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
rejected.why: Not supported by the presence of pus discharge and lack of specific mention of a mucocele in imaging studies

rejected.label: Sinusitis-induced orbital abscess
rejected.why: The absence of any abnormal lesions in the orbital tissue on MRI makes this diagnosis less likely
